subject.title: [Bug]: Subagents can appear completed before the underlying delegated work is actually finished

question: Should subagent completion wait for child-owned background exec/process sessions, or should those sessions be reported as separate still-running work after the subagent agent turn completes?
rationale: Both behaviors are plausible product contracts, and current docs make agent lifecycle authoritative while the issue expects delegated work liveness to affect completion state.

options.title: Surface background work separately
options.body: Keep agent-run lifecycle as the terminal subagent turn but make active child-owned process sessions visible in tasks/subagents status and parent handoff so users are not told all delegated work is done.

options.title: Block completion on child process liveness
options.body: Treat scoped background process sessions as part of the subagent completion gate with timeout and escape rules for intentional long-running processes.

options.title: Document current semantics
options.body: Close the behavioral gap by documenting that subagent completion means the child agent turn ended, while background processes must be tracked through process/task status.

recommendation.title: Surface background work separately
recommendation.body: Keep agent-run lifecycle as the terminal subagent turn but make active child-owned process sessions visible in tasks/subagents status and parent handoff so users are not told all delegated work is done.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent subagent lifecycle and cleanup work is closest to the contract boundary that needs a product/runtime decision.
